'''Karl von der Mühll''' (September 13, 1841, in [[Basel]], [[Switzerland]] – May 9, 1912, in Basel) was a Swiss mathematician and physicist.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Wichers|first=Hermann|title=Karl von der Mühll|url=https://hls-dhs-dss.ch/fr/articles/032104/2009-01-14/|website=Dictionaire Historique de la Suisse}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite book|last=Knapp|first=Martin|title=Verhandlungen der Schweizerischen Naturforschenden Gesellschaft. Prof. Dr. Karl Von der Mühll-His. 1841–1912.|publisher=Societe Generale d'Imprimerie, Geneve|year=1912|location=Geneva|pages=93–106}}</ref>

He was born into the [[Von der Mühll]] family, of the Basel [[Patrician (post-Roman Europe)|patriciate]] (see [[Daig (Switzerland)|Daig]]), to Karl Georg and Emilie Merian, of the [[Merian family]], a granddaughter of [[Peter Merian]].

After graduating from high school in 1859, Von der Mühll studied natural sciences and mathematics at the [[University of Basel]], with amongst others, [[Gustav Heinrich Wiedemann]], and from 1861 studied at the [[University of Göttingen|Georg-August University]] in Göttingen with [[Bernhard Riemann]], [[Wilhelm Eduard Weber]], [[Wilhelm Klinkerfues]] and [[Friedrich Wöhler]]. From 1863, he continued his studies at the [[University of Königsberg|Albertus University]] in Königsberg, where he turned to mathematical physics under [[Franz Ernst Neumann]] and received his doctorate in 1866. He also studied there with the mathematician [[Friedrich Julius Richelot]]. In 1866/67, he studied at the [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]] in Paris. Shortly after, in 1868, he completed his studies in [[Leipzig]] in mathematical physics and in 1872 he became an associate professor at the university.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professorenkatalog der Universität Leipzig - Die Professoren-Datenbank für Leipzig|url=https://research.uni-leipzig.de/catalogus-professorum-lipsiensium/leipzig/Muehll_927/|access-date=2020-08-27|website=research.uni-leipzig.de}}</ref> In 1889, he left Leipzig for Basel and became associate professor and in 1890 professor for mathematical physics at Basel University. In 1896, he became the university's financial administrator (''Curator fiscorum academicorum''). In the academic years 1895/96 and 1910/11, he was [[Rector (academia)|rector]] of the university. In 1887, he was elected a member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref name=":1" />

He was president of the Swiss Euler Commission (and thus editor of [[Leonhard Euler]]'s works) and published Franz Neumann's lectures on electrical currents in 1884. From 1872 he was co-editor of the ''[[Mathematische Annalen]]''.<ref name=":2">{{Cite book|last=His|first=Eduard|title=Basler Gelehrte des 19. Jahrhunderts|publisher=Schwab, Basel|year=1941|location=Basel|pages=239–242}}</ref>

In 1875 he married Katharina His, daughter of Eduard His, also of the Basel Daig.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

Having suffered from several bouts of depression throughout his life, Von der Mühll committed suicide in 1912 and is buried in the Wolfgottesacker cemetery in Basel.<ref name=":2" />
